displayPattern: Amber status LED on a Carrier 59SC5: 1 short flash, then 2 long flashes (code 12)
meaning: Blower on after power-up. The service label calls this normal operation. The blower runs for 90 seconds if the furnace was powered up during a call for heat, or if that call opened during the blower on-delay.
causes: 115 VAC or 24 VAC power came up while a call for heat was present (R-W closed)
The heat call opened during the blower on-delay
diySteps: Count 1 short flash and 2 long flashes. If the blower stops after about 90 seconds, that matches the label
If the blower never stops, the call for heat may still be closed. A technician checks that circuit. Code 12 is not a limit lockout and not an ignition lockout
proAdvice: Call a licensed HVAC technician if the blower runs and the burners never light, or if the blower does not stop. A 90-second run right after power returns is the normal code 12 the label describes.
safetyNote: If you smell gas, do not touch any electrical switch or use a phone in the building; leave immediately and call your gas supplier from outside. Turn off electrical power at the furnace switch or breaker before opening any panel, and never bypass or jumper a limit, rollout or pressure switch. Gas valve, burner, venting, wiring and control-board work should be done by a licensed HVAC technician.
sourceTitle: Carrier 59SC5A installation, start-up, operating and service instructions (Catalog No. 59SC5A-01SI), Fig. 55 service label. Read 2026-11-07
